outcome: Transmission of MDRO+ (colonization or invasion with genetically indistinguishable bacteria)
cohort: The study included 434 infants admitted to a level III NICU who remained on the ward for 48 hours or more and received one or more screenings for multidrug-resistant organisms.
finding: Bacterial sequencing accurately detected bacterial transmission events in NICU infants, revealing that increased full-time nurse staffing and prior antibiotic use decreased transmission risk, while vascular catheter use increased it.
